kits.asmKit:
;; Xenon's input and output routines for x86-64 Linux assembly (NASM, Intel syntax).
;;
;; The website adds the routines a program calls to the end of the program before assembling it, so a lesson can
;; say `call print_int` without first teaching how numbers become text. Each routine is a block below that starts
;; with a ";; @name: needs" line; the website copies only the blocks a program uses (and what they need), and never
;; one the program defines itself.
;;
;; Every routine follows the System V calling convention, as C functions on Linux do:
;;   arguments in rdi, rsi, rdx; the result in rax;
;;   rbx, rbp, rsp and r12 to r15 are as they were; rax, rcx, rdx, rsi, rdi and r8 to r11 may change.

;; @xenon_out:
        section .data
xenon_fd:       dd      1               ; where print_* write: 1 is standard output, 2 standard error
        section .text
;; xenon_write: rsi = bytes, rdx = how many. Writes them all to [xenon_fd].
xenon_write:
        push    rbx
        push    r12
        mov     rbx, rsi
        mov     r12, rdx
.more:  test    r12, r12
        jle     .done
        mov     eax, 1                  ; system call 1: write
        mov     edi, [rel xenon_fd]
        mov     rsi, rbx
        mov     rdx, r12
        syscall
        test    rax, rax
        jle     .done                   ; an error: give up quietly
        add     rbx, rax
        sub     r12, rax
        jmp     .more
.done:  pop     r12
        pop     rbx
        ret

;; @print_str: xenon_out
;; print_str: rdi = the address of a zero-terminated string.
print_str:
        mov     rsi, rdi
        xor     edx, edx
.len:   cmp     byte [rsi + rdx], 0
        je      .go
        inc     rdx
        jmp     .len
.go:    jmp     xenon_write

;; @print_char: xenon_out
;; print_char: dil = one character.
print_char:
        sub     rsp, 24
        mov     [rsp], dil
        mov     rsi, rsp
        mov     edx, 1
        call    xenon_write
        add     rsp, 24
        ret

;; @print_newline: print_char
print_newline:
        mov     edi, 10
        jmp     print_char

;; @print_uint: xenon_out
;; print_uint: rdi = an unsigned number, printed in decimal.
print_uint:
        sub     rsp, 40
        lea     rsi, [rsp + 32]         ; digits are written backwards from here
        mov     rax, rdi
        mov     ecx, 10
.digit: xor     edx, edx
        div     rcx                     ; rax = rax / 10, rdx = the last digit
        add     dl, '0'
        dec     rsi
        mov     [rsi], dl
        test    rax, rax
        jnz     .digit
        lea     rdx, [rsp + 32]
        sub     rdx, rsi
        call    xenon_write
        add     rsp, 40
        ret

;; @print_int: print_uint print_char
;; print_int: rdi = a signed number, printed in decimal (with a minus sign when negative).
print_int:
        test    rdi, rdi
        jns     print_uint
        push    rdi
        mov     edi, '-'
        call    print_char
        pop     rdi
        neg     rdi                     ; the most negative number stays itself, and prints right as unsigned
        jmp     print_uint

;; @print_hex: xenon_out
;; print_hex: rdi = a number, printed as 0x followed by its hexadecimal digits (lower case, no leading zeros).
print_hex:
        sub     rsp, 40
        lea     rsi, [rsp + 32]
        mov     rax, rdi
.digit: mov     edx, eax
        and     edx, 15
        cmp     edx, 10
        jb      .num
        add     edx, 'a' - '0' - 10
.num:   add     edx, '0'
        dec     rsi
        mov     [rsi], dl
        shr     rax, 4
        jnz     .digit
        dec     rsi
        mov     byte [rsi], 'x'
        dec     rsi
        mov     byte [rsi], '0'
        lea     rdx, [rsp + 32]
        sub     rdx, rsi
        call    xenon_write
        add     rsp, 40
        ret

;; @print_bin: xenon_out
;; print_bin: rdi = a number, rsi = how many of its lowest bits to show (1 to 64). Prints them, highest first.
print_bin:
        sub     rsp, 72
        mov     rcx, rsi
        cmp     rcx, 1
        jge     .low
        mov     ecx, 1
.low:   cmp     rcx, 64
        jle     .ok
        mov     ecx, 64
.ok:    mov     rdx, rcx                ; the length
        lea     rsi, [rsp]
        xor     r8d, r8d
.bit:   dec     rcx
        bt      rdi, rcx
        setc    al
        add     al, '0'
        mov     [rsi + r8], al
        inc     r8
        test    rcx, rcx
        jnz     .bit
        call    xenon_write
        add     rsp, 72
        ret

;; @xenon_in:
        section .bss
xenon_inbuf:    resb    4096
        section .data
xenon_inpos:    dq      0
xenon_inlen:    dq      0
xenon_back:     dq      -2              ; a character put back, or -2 for none
        section .text
;; xenon_getc: returns the next byte of standard input in rax, or -1 at the end.
xenon_getc:
        mov     rax, [rel xenon_back]
        cmp     rax, -2
        je      .buffer
        mov     qword [rel xenon_back], -2
        ret
.buffer:
        mov     rax, [rel xenon_inpos]
        cmp     rax, [rel xenon_inlen]
        jb      .take
        xor     eax, eax                ; system call 0: read
        xor     edi, edi
        lea     rsi, [rel xenon_inbuf]
        mov     edx, 4096
        syscall
        test    rax, rax
        jle     .end
        mov     [rel xenon_inlen], rax
        mov     qword [rel xenon_inpos], 0
        xor     eax, eax
.take:  lea     rcx, [rel xenon_inbuf]
        movzx   ecx, byte [rcx + rax]
        inc     rax
        mov     [rel xenon_inpos], rax
        mov     eax, ecx
        ret
.end:   mov     rax, -1
        ret
;; xenon_ungetc: rdi = a byte to give back to the next xenon_getc.
xenon_ungetc:
        mov     [rel xenon_back], rdi
        ret

;; @read_char: xenon_in
;; read_char: returns the next character of the input in rax, or -1 at the end of the input.
read_char:
        jmp     xenon_getc

;; @read_int: xenon_in
;; read_int: skips spaces and new lines, then reads a whole number (a minus sign is allowed).
;; Returns the number in rax and 1 in rdx, or 0 in both when the input has no number left.
read_int:
        push    rbx
        push    r12
.skip:  call    xenon_getc
        cmp     rax, -1
        je      .none
        cmp     rax, ' '
        je      .skip
        cmp     rax, 9
        jb      .start
        cmp     rax, 13
        jbe     .skip
.start: xor     r12d, r12d              ; 1 when negative
        cmp     rax, '-'
        jne     .first
        mov     r12d, 1
        call    xenon_getc
.first: lea     rcx, [rax - '0']
        cmp     rcx, 9
        ja      .bad                    ; not a digit: there is no number here
        xor     ebx, ebx
.digit: imul    rbx, rbx, 10
        lea     rcx, [rax - '0']
        add     rbx, rcx
        call    xenon_getc
        lea     rcx, [rax - '0']
        cmp     rcx, 9
        jbe     .digit
        mov     rdi, rax                ; the character after the number is kept for the next read
        call    xenon_ungetc
        mov     rax, rbx
        test    r12d, r12d
        jz      .done
        neg     rax
.done:  mov     edx, 1
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
        ret
.bad:   mov     rdi, rax
        call    xenon_ungetc
.none:  xor     eax, eax
        xor     edx, edx
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
        ret

;; @read_line: xenon_in
;; read_line: rdi = a buffer, rsi = its size. Reads one line into it, without the new line, and ends it with a 0
;; byte. Returns the line's length in rax, or -1 when the input has ended and there was nothing left to read.
;; A line longer than the buffer is cut short; the rest of it is skipped.
read_line:
        push    rbx
        push    r12
        push    r13
        mov     rbx, rdi
        lea     r12, [rsi - 1]          ; room for the characters, leaving one byte for the 0
        xor     r13d, r13d              ; how many were stored
        call    xenon_getc
        cmp     rax, -1
        jne     .have
        mov     byte [rbx], 0
        mov     rax, -1
        jmp     .out
.next:  call    xenon_getc
.have:  cmp     rax, -1
        je      .end
        cmp     rax, 10
        je      .end
        cmp     rax, 13
        je      .next                   ; a Windows line end: the \r is dropped
        cmp     r13, r12
        jae     .next                   ; full: keep reading to the end of the line
        mov     [rbx + r13], al
        inc     r13
        jmp     .next
.end:   mov     byte [rbx + r13], 0
        mov     rax, r13
.out:   pop     r13
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
        ret
kits.lua:
-- Xenon's runner for Lua on the website. Compiler Explorer runs this file; the learner's files sit next to it.
-- It does one of three jobs, chosen by the table the website adds at the end (xenon_main{...}):
--   "check"  load every .lua file and report syntax errors, without running anything
--   "run"    run the entry file like `lua main.lua`; with interactive, stop and say so when input runs out
--   "unit"   run the solution file, then the tests written against it, and report each one
-- Reports and errors use simple text lines the website reads; nothing here is shown to the learner as-is.

local MARK_INPUT = "<<" .. "xenon:needs-input" .. ">>"
local MARK_SYNTAX = "<<" .. "xenon:syntax" .. ">>"
local USER = {}          -- the learner's .lua files, by name
local raw_traceback = debug.traceback

local real_write, real_print = io.write, print
local stdout, stderr = io.stdout, io.stderr

-- ------------------------------------------------------------ errors and tracebacks

-- A traceback the learner's own code asks for (debug.traceback) leaves out this runner's frames, which sit
-- below the learner's main chunk: lines in this file (output.s) and the C calls that started the main chunk.
local function tidy_traceback(tb)
  local lines, dropped = {}, false
  for line in (tb .. "\n"):gmatch("(.-)\n") do
    if line:find("output%.s:") or (dropped and line:find("^%s*%(%.%.%.tail calls%.%.%.%)$")) then
      dropped = true
    else
      lines[#lines + 1] = line
      dropped = false
    end
  end
  local last_main
  for i, line in ipairs(lines) do if line:find(": in main chunk$") then last_main = i end end
  if last_main then
    for i = #lines, last_main + 1, -1 do
      if lines[i]:find("^%s*%[C%]: in ") then table.remove(lines, i) end
    end
  end
  return table.concat(lines, "\n")
end

local function install_tidy_traceback()
  debug.traceback = function(a, b, c)
    if type(a) == "thread" then
      local tb = raw_traceback(a, b, c)
      return type(tb) == "string" and tidy_traceback(tb) or tb
    end
    if a ~= nil and type(a) ~= "string" and type(a) ~= "number" then return a end
    -- Levels count from the caller. Called normally, this wrapper is one extra frame; called as a tail call
    -- (return debug.traceback(...)), it took the caller's place, as the real C function would not have.
    local tail = debug.getinfo(1, "t").istailcall
    return tidy_traceback(raw_traceback(a, (b or 1) + (tail and 0 or 1)))
  end
end

-- A traceback with only the learner's own frames: not this runner.
local function user_traceback(message, level)
  local tb = raw_traceback("", (level or 1) + 1)
  local keep = {}
  for line in tb:gmatch("[^\n]+") do
    local trimmed = line:gsub("^%s+", "")
    if trimmed ~= "stack traceback:" and not line:find("output%.s") and not line:find("xenon_main") and not line:find("in function 'xpcall'")
       and not line:find("in function 'pcall'") and not line:find("%[C%]: in %?") then
      keep[#keep + 1] = "\t" .. trimmed
    end
  end
  local text = tostring(message)
  if #keep > 0 then text = text .. "\nstack traceback:\n" .. table.concat(keep, "\n") end
  return text
end

local function syntax_errors(names)
  local found = {}
  for _, name in ipairs(names) do
    local fh = io.open(name, "r")
    if fh then
      local text = fh:read("a")
      fh:close()
      local ok, err = load(text, "@" .. name, "t")
      if not ok then
        local file, line, msg = tostring(err):match("^(.-):(%d+): (.*)$")
        if file then found[#found + 1] = file .. ":" .. line .. ":1: error: " .. msg
        else found[#found + 1] = name .. ":1:1: error: " .. tostring(err) end
      end
    end
  end
  return found
end

local function load_file(name)
  local fh = assert(io.open(name, "r"))
  local text = fh:read("a")
  fh:close()
  return assert(load(text, "@" .. name, "t"))
end

-- ------------------------------------------------------------ input that waits

local function stop_for_input()
  stdout:flush()
  stdout:write(MARK_INPUT)
  stdout:flush()
  stderr:flush()
  os.exit(0)
end

local function install_waiting_input()
  local meta = getmetatable(io.stdin).__index
  local raw_read, raw_lines = meta.read, meta.lines
  local stdin = io.stdin
  local function at_end() return raw_read(stdin, 0) == nil end
  local function waiting_read(fh, ...)
    if fh ~= stdin then return raw_read(fh, ...) end
    local formats = table.pack(...)
    if formats.n == 0 then formats = { "l", n = 1 } end
    for i = 1, formats.n do
      local f = formats[i]
      if type(f) == "string" and f:gsub("^%*", ""):sub(1, 1) == "a" then stop_for_input() end
    end
    if at_end() then stop_for_input() end
    local results = table.pack(raw_read(fh, table.unpack(formats, 1, formats.n)))
    for i = 1, formats.n do
      if results[i] == nil and at_end() then stop_for_input() end
    end
    return table.unpack(results, 1, results.n)
  end
  meta.read = waiting_read
  meta.lines = function(fh, ...)
    if fh ~= stdin then return raw_lines(fh, ...) end
    local formats = table.pack(...)
    return function() return waiting_read(fh, table.unpack(formats, 1, formats.n)) end
  end
  io.read = function(...) return waiting_read(io.input(), ...) end
  local real_lines = io.lines
  io.lines = function(name, ...)
    if name == nil then return meta.lines(stdin, ...) end
    return real_lines(name, ...)
  end
end

-- ------------------------------------------------------------ running a program

local function run(entry, interactive, args)
  if interactive then install_waiting_input() end
  arg = { [0] = entry }
  for i, a in ipairs(args or {}) do arg[i] = a end
  local chunk = load_file(entry)
  local ok, err = xpcall(chunk, function(e) return user_traceback(e, 1) end, table.unpack(arg))
  stdout:flush()
  if not ok then
    stderr:write("lua: ", tostring(err), "\n")
    stderr:flush()
    os.exit(1)
  end
end

-- ------------------------------------------------------------ the test kit

local tests, failures = {}, {}

local function esc(text)
  return (tostring(text):gsub("\\", "\\\\"):gsub("\n", "\\n"):gsub("\t", "\\t"))
end

local function test_line()
  for level = 2, 60 do
    local info = debug.getinfo(level, "Sl")
    if not info then break end
    if info.source == "@the tests" then return info.currentline end
  end
  return nil
end

local function fail(message)
  local line = test_line()
  failures[#failures + 1] = message .. (line and (" (line " .. line .. ")") or "")
end

local function show(value, depth, seen)
  depth, seen = depth or 0, seen or {}
  local t = type(value)
  if t == "string" then return (string.format("%q", value):gsub("\\\n", "\\n")) end
  if t == "number" then
    if math.type(value) == "float" and value == math.floor(value) and math.abs(value) < 1e15 then return string.format("%.1f", value) end
    return tostring(value)
  end
  if t ~= "table" then return tostring(value) end
  if seen[value] then return "{...}" end
  if depth > 3 then return "{...}" end
  seen[value] = true
  local parts, n = {}, #value
  for i = 1, n do parts[#parts + 1] = show(value[i], depth + 1, seen) end
  local keys = {}
  for k in pairs(value) do
    if not (math.type(k) == "integer" and k >= 1 and k <= n) then keys[#keys + 1] = k end
  end
  table.sort(keys, function(a, b) return tostring(a) < tostring(b) end)
  for _, k in ipairs(keys) do
    local key = type(k) == "string" and k:match("^[%a_][%w_]*$") and k or ("[" .. show(k, depth + 1, seen) .. "]")
    parts[#parts + 1] = key .. " = " .. show(value[k], depth + 1, seen)
  end
  seen[value] = nil
  if #parts > 40 then parts = { table.concat(parts, ", ", 1, 40) .. ", ..." } end
  return "{" .. table.concat(parts, ", ") .. "}"
end

local function same(a, b, seen)
  if a == b then return true end
  if type(a) == "number" and type(b) == "number" then
    return math.abs(a - b) <= 1e-9 * math.max(1.0, math.abs(b))
  end
  if type(a) ~= "table" or type(b) ~= "table" then return false end
  seen = seen or {}
  if seen[a] == b then return true end
  seen[a] = b
  for k, v in pairs(a) do if not same(v, b[k], seen) then return false end end
  for k in pairs(b) do if a[k] == nil then return false end end
  return true
end

function test(name, fn)
  tests[#tests + 1] = { name = tostring(name), fn = fn }
end

function check(condition, message)
  if not condition then fail(message or "check(...) was false") end
end

function check_eq(actual, expected, message)
  if not same(actual, expected) then
    fail("gave " .. show(actual) .. ", expected " .. show(expected) .. (message and (" (" .. tostring(message) .. ")") or ""))
  end
end

function check_near(actual, expected, eps)
  eps = eps or 1e-6
  if type(actual) ~= "number" or math.abs(actual - expected) > eps then
    fail("gave " .. show(actual) .. ", expected about " .. show(expected))
  end
end

-- check_error(fn, ...) passes when calling fn(...) raises an error.
-- check_error_like(text, fn, ...) also wants that text somewhere in the error message.
local function error_text(e)
  return type(e) == "table" and (rawget(e, "message") or show(e)) or tostring(e)
end
function check_error(fn, ...)
  local ok = pcall(fn, ...)
  if ok then fail("did not raise an error") end
end
function check_error_like(text, fn, ...)
  local ok, err = pcall(fn, ...)
  if ok then fail("did not raise an error (expected one mentioning " .. show(text) .. ")")
  elseif not error_text(err):find(text, 1, true) then fail("raised " .. show(error_text(err)) .. ", expected an error mentioning " .. show(text)) end
end

-- check_output(fn, expected) runs fn() and compares what it printed (print and io.write).
local function tidy(s)
  local lines = {}
  for line in (tostring(s):gsub("\r\n", "\n") .. "\n"):gmatch("(.-)\n") do lines[#lines + 1] = (line:gsub("%s+$", "")) end
  return (table.concat(lines, "\n"):gsub("\n+$", ""))
end
function check_output(fn, expected)
  local buf = {}
  local function put(...)
    for i = 1, select("#", ...) do buf[#buf + 1] = tostring((select(i, ...))) end
  end
  print = function(...)
    local n = select("#", ...)
    for i = 1, n do buf[#buf + 1] = tostring((select(i, ...))); if i < n then buf[#buf + 1] = "\t" end end
    buf[#buf + 1] = "\n"
  end
  io.write = function(...) put(...); return io.stdout end
  local ok, err = pcall(fn)
  print, io.write = real_print, real_write
  if not ok then error(err, 0) end
  local got = tidy(table.concat(buf))
  if got ~= tidy(expected) then fail("printed " .. show(got) .. ", expected " .. show(tidy(expected))) end
end

local function where_in_user(tb)
  for line in tostring(tb):gmatch("[^\n]+") do
    local file, num = line:match("([%w_%-%./]+%.lua):(%d+):")
    if file then file = file:gsub("^%./", "") end
    if file and USER[file] then return " in " .. file .. " line " .. num end
  end
  return ""
end

local function unit(entry, tests_file)
  -- The solution runs first. A module that returns a table also lends its functions to the tests.
  local chunk = load_file(entry)
  local ok, result = xpcall(chunk, function(e) return user_traceback(e, 1) end)
  if not ok then
    stderr:write("lua: ", tostring(result), "\n")
    os.exit(1)
  end
  if type(result) == "table" then
    solution = result
    for k, v in pairs(result) do if type(k) == "string" and rawget(_G, k) == nil then _G[k] = v end end
    local name = entry:gsub("%.lua$", "")
    package.loaded[name] = result
  end
  local fh = assert(io.open(tests_file, "r"))
  local tests_text = fh:read("a")
  fh:close()
  local tests_chunk = assert(load(tests_text, "@the tests", "t"))
  local loaded, problem = xpcall(tests_chunk, function(e) return user_traceback(e, 1) end)
  if not loaded then
    stderr:write("lua: ", tostring(problem), "\n")
    os.exit(1)
  end

  local failed = 0
  for _, t in ipairs(tests) do
    stderr:write("B\t", esc(t.name), "\n")
    stderr:flush()
    failures = {}
    local passed, err = xpcall(t.fn, function(e)
      local where = where_in_user(raw_traceback("", 2))
      local message = error_text(e)
      local line = message:match("^the tests:(%d+): ")
      if line then return message:gsub("^the tests:%d+: ", "") .. " (line " .. line .. ")" end
      return "raised an error: " .. message .. (message:find("%.lua:%d+:") and "" or where)
    end)
    if not passed then failures[#failures + 1] = err end
    if #failures > 0 then
      failed = failed + 1
      stderr:write("F\t", esc(t.name), "\t", esc(table.concat(failures, "; ")), "\n")
    else
      stderr:write("P\t", esc(t.name), "\n")
    end
    stderr:flush()
  end
  stdout:flush()
  stderr:write("E\t", failed, "\n")
  stderr:flush()
end

function xenon_main(job)
  local names = {}
  for _, name in ipairs(job.files or {}) do USER[name] = true; names[#names + 1] = name end
  local errors = syntax_errors(names)
  if #errors > 0 then
    stdout:write(MARK_SYNTAX, "\n", table.concat(errors, "\n"), "\n")
    stdout:flush()
    os.exit(3)
  end
  if job.mode == "check" then return end
  install_tidy_traceback()
  if job.mode == "unit" then
    local tests_errors = syntax_errors({ job.tests })
    if #tests_errors > 0 then
      stdout:write(MARK_SYNTAX, "\n", (table.concat(tests_errors, "\n"):gsub(job.tests, "the tests")), "\n")
      os.exit(3)
    end
    unit(job.entry, job.tests)
  else
    run(job.entry, job.interactive, job.args)
  end
end
